reason: The text depicts and reinforces multiple hierarchical structures throughout the narrative. Most prominently: (1) Divine hierarchy—God commands Moses who leads the Israelites, establishing God > Moses > People as the authority structure; (2) The people repeatedly turn to Moses for guidance and reassurance, acknowledging his leadership role; (3) God's instruction to Moses ('what are you crying to me for? Tell the Israelites to move on') and Moses' corresponding authority to direct the people demonstrates delegated command authority; (4) The narrative concludes by affirming the people's belief 'in the Lord and in Moses his servant,' explicitly endorsing the hierarchical relationship; (5) The successful outcome (deliverance) is presented as contingent upon respecting this hierarchical chain of command—the people are saved when they follow Moses' direction. The Pharaoh's opposing hierarchy (Pharaoh > Egyptian forces) is contrasted unfavorably, further emphasizing the legitimacy of the God-Moses-Israel hierarchy.
